knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 5.1.8
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Which statement correctly describes how Empirical Bayes obtains structural parameters differently from a fully specified Bayesian prior and names the premium derived?
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: EB estimates overall mean and process variance components from collective experience, then forms credibility premium. Same assumptions as fully Bayesian is incorrect.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Estimate structurals from collective data; premium Ẑ X̄ + (1-Ẑ) μ̂.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Treating EB as identical assumptions or single-claim update.

choices.label: Empirical Bayes estimates structural parameters from collective data rather than treating them as fully specified by a prior alone. The credibility premium Ẑ times X̄ + (1 minus Ẑ) times μ-hat follows after plugging estimated structural parameters into the credibility formula.
Empirical Bayes and fully Bayesian credibility always use identical assumptions for structural parameters.
Empirical Bayes obtains the premium only by applying Bayes' theorem to a single claim; collective data never enter.
Empirical Bayes means choosing Z = 1 always because data estimate full credibility automatically.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 5.1.8
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Which statement correctly outlines the Empirical Bayes move to obtain a credibility premium when structural parameters are unknown?
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: EB pipeline: estimate structurals, plug into credibility form, compute premium. That calculation differs from the contrast LO about assumptions.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Estimate structurals from collective data; plug into Z and mu; form premium.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Treating one EB premium calculation as finishing Bayes versus EB contrast.

choices.label: Estimate structural parameters (for example overall mean and process or variance components) from the collective data, plug them into the credibility formula to get Ẑ and μ̂, then form Ẑ times X̄ + (1 minus Ẑ) times μ-hat for the risk. Computing one EB premium is not the same task as contrasting assumption sets of Bayes versus EB.
Computing one EB premium finishes explaining how Bayesian and Empirical Bayes differ in assumptions.
Empirical Bayes requires a fully specified prior before any data; collective estimation is unnecessary.
Structural parameters are set to sample proportions only; no credibility formula is used afterward.

worked_example.title: Empirical Bayes premium with estimated structurals
worked_example.problem_statement: Under Empirical Bayes, structural parameters are estimated from collective data: μ̂ = £500 and k̂ = 10. A risk has n = 5 years with X̄ = £700. Compute Ẑ = n/(n+k̂) and the EB credibility premium P = Ẑ X̄ + (1 − Ẑ) μ̂.
worked_example.attempt_before_reveal: CMP closed. Form Ẑ = 5/(5+10), then blend X̄ with μ̂.

steps.label: Estimated credibility factor
steps.explanation: Empirical Bayes replaces a fully specified prior's structurals with estimates from the collective portfolio.

steps.label: EB premium
steps.explanation: The premium formula matches classical credibility, with estimated Z and μ.

steps.label: Source of structurals
steps.attempt_cue: Contrast EB with a fully Bayesian prior specification.
steps.explanation: EB estimates μ and k from data; a fully Bayesian analysis would take them from an explicit prior structure.
steps.calculation: Structurals μ̂, k̂ from collective data (not a fixed prior)

worked_example.common_pitfall: Using the fully Bayesian k = 3 from a different exercise instead of the collective estimate k̂ = 10, which would incorrectly give Z = 5/8 and a different premium.
